newsitem.title: USA: Traders see early word on Conrail deal.
newsitem.headline: Traders see early word on Conrail deal.

text.p: Takeover stock traders said Friday they were anticipating an early settlement to negotiations over the fate of Conrail Inc, although questions remained over the final structure of the deal.
"We're just trying to figure out this last chapter," said one trader. "Our sense is it's pretty imminent," he said.

Conrail spokesman Bob Libkind, asked to comment on market and industry rumors the company was having a board meeting Friday, said he was unaware of any meeting. "Obviously if we have any announcement we will put it out," he said.
"It might be today, but I've been fooled before," he said.

Traders and analysts said a complex array of alternatives must be considered in weighing any final deal to divide Conrail between CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp and end a fierce takeover battle over the railroad.

"They're talking about a very, very complex deal, both from a legal standpoint and from a financial standpoint," Prudential Securities analyst Brian Routledge said. "My understanding is they've got three or four potential scenarios."

Conrail on Monday said it had authorized its management to negotiate a revised merger agreement with CSX, based on obtaining $115 cash per share, or about $10.3 billion, for its shareholders as soon as possible.
The announcement set the stage for a deal to carve up Conrail between the two rival suitors, as acknowledged by Conrail Chairman David LeVan in a telecast address to employees Wednesday.

What the railroads have to work out is not just who gets what portions of Conrail, but how to set up a deal that would honor promises for a quick payment to shareholders while allowing for a potentially time-consuming federal regulatory approvals process, Routledge said.
"The major complication that I see is the fact that somehow you're going to have to put up (the money) well before you get any benefits," he said.
Norfolk Southern spokesman Frank Brown said additional negotiations and technical work would probably follow any announcement from Conrail on the deal.
But he said the announcement would make clear the outlines of a final deal.
